content:
Formula: Maxwell-Faraday Equation
Exact Expression: \nabla \times \mathbf{E} = -\frac{\partial \mathbf{B}}{\partial t}
Definitions: Fundamental Maxwell equation stating that a time-varying magnetic field induces an orthogonal circulating non-conservative electric field.
Derivation/Reference: Michael Faraday experimental law (1831); James Clerk Maxwell differential formulation (1861)
Example: Transformer coil: EMF = -N (d Phi / dt) according to Lenz's law opposing flux changes
Domain: electromagnetism
Assumptions: Valid in classical electrodynamics across all inertial reference frames
Common Errors: Omitting minus sign which enforces Lenz's law and energy conservation
subject: Maxwell-Faraday Equation
